name: napalm-canonical-bgp-configuration-diagnostics
instr:
NAPALM cannot explain cross-vendor BGP normalization without changing its established getter. Add portable diagnostics for retrieval, comparison, compliance validation, mock replay, and command-line reporting without exposing authentication material.

Each supported IOS, IOS-XR, IOS-XR NETCONF, Junos, and EOS diagnostic call returns one typed BGPDiagnosticSnapshot containing ordinary configuration and canonically ordered observations and warnings. Apply group and neighbor filters throughout; neighbor-only requests without a group retain established behavior. Equivalent prefix-limit values from IOS, IOS-XR, IOS-XR NETCONF, and Junos share canonical address-family paths and values. Keep missing, empty, malformed, and conversion-failed fields distinct. Recoverable defects warn without discarding valid neighboring configuration; native transport failures remain exceptions.

`diff_bgp_diagnostics` deterministically reports added, removed, changed, and warning differences by canonical semantic path. Snapshots and differences hide BGP authentication secrets while reporting protected-field normalization. They round-trip through plain dictionaries without vendor objects, using schema version 1 and canonical ordering; diagnostic collections are tuples in the typed objects and lists in their plain-dictionary form. Validation command-line reports use deterministic path-and-kind ordering and explicitly indicate semantic differences. The mock driver validates arguments, rejects diagnostic
